data.reason:
The KPI's main goal is town-wide on_time_deliveries, with p95_wait_s, max_wait_s and unfinished as watched goals (K1). Option 1 raises on-time from 272.6 to 273.6 (+1.0, 4/5 seeds improved) and passes check, the constitution, the KPI conditions and the objective gate. That is the kind of consistent evidence D2 lacked (2/5).

It also improves every customer-facing metric. Late falls from 2.0 to 1.0, p95_wait_s from 90.0 to 83.0 and max_wait_s from 212 to 154. Unfinished stays 0.0, blocked s falls from 1102 to 915 and the lowest on-time rate rises from 0.98 to 0.99.

Option 2 is unanimous and harmless, but its gain (+0.6, 2/5 seeds) is not established. It leaves max_wait_s at 212 and gives C only 68.8 -> 69.5. That is too small to count as meeting the D1 promise, so choosing it would mostly be symbolic, at the cost of customers' worst-case waits. Keep gives no one anything.

I follow the LLM's recommendation. I acknowledge that I am choosing against C's no vote. C's loss here (68.8 -> 66.3, -2.5) is small compared with D1, and A (+1.0) and B (+1.2) support the change. Customers, who do not vote, gain the most. No contract change is involved, so customers' promised times are unaffected.

This is the fourth period without a real mitigation for C. I take responsibility on behalf of the operator for not delivering it here. I commit to measuring a targeted mitigation for C next period instead of trading customer tail waits for it.

The main risk is road violations rising from 29.6 to 32.6. Their cause has been flagged since D1 and is still unexamined. This is a reversible rule change, and I will revert or try an intermediate value (e.g. 55s) if the violations prove safety-relevant.
assumptions: The same-seed averages are representative of next period's busy + rush conditions.
The additional road violations (+3.0) are not safety-critical, since the change passed the constitution.
C's utility loss of 2.5 will not trigger a material drop in C's cooperation.
The rule change can be reverted next period if needed.
unknowns: Why road violations rise when the hold limit is shortened, and whether they matter for safety.
Per-seed values of p95_wait_s and max_wait_s.
Whether 55s keeps most of the customer gain with a smaller cost to C and fewer violations.
What targeted mitigation for C (compensation or a fix for C's bottleneck) is feasible, and what it would cost customers.
How C will respond to losing another vote, and next period's demand level.
